label: rem:confinement-nucleon-unit
title: Nucleon-as-unit justification from LP confinement proof
html:
The confinement LP proof and the Gram degeneracy theorem jointly justify treating nucleons as atomic units in the transfer matrix chain. The proof is purely algebraic. We use LP duality, Gram matrix eigenstructure, and braid group realizability. No physics assumptions enter.

Statement. The inter-nucleon transfer matrix uses nucleon strand types p, n with crossing coefficients pp: (1,0), nn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}), pn: (1,-h_{\mathrm{A}}/2), without resolving the internal quark structure. This is exact because:

  1. LP confinement proves that the Borromean operator B_3 = (\sigma_0\sigma_1^{-1})^3 traps the quark NF coefficients in the Frobenius cone G\vec{x} \geq 0. No quark subset can unbind.
  2. Gram degeneracy (\det G = 0 under the production convention D, the (1^3) block being the radical) shows that energy minimization has no interior strict minimum on the full six-dimensional NF span; the minimisation is well posed only on the quotient by the radical, where it attains its minimum at \mathrm{tr}_M = 0. The earlier statement here, "Gram indefiniteness (\det G < 0)", quoted the convention-C determinant -0.18920521914403668 on the bilinear pairing and is withdrawn on both counts (2026-08-09). Confinement at \mathrm{tr}_M \approx 1 is topological, forced by the braid group realizability constraint B_3.
  3. Consequence for the transfer matrix: Since quarks cannot unbind, the nucleon's internal braid structure acts as a rigid unit. The inter-nucleon crossing between nucleon i and nucleon j depends only on the nucleon types, not on the quark arrangement. The transfer matrix Skein polynomial P = \prod_i \hat{V}_i captures the full inter-nucleon physics at the nucleon level.
  4. Error bound: The nucleon-as-unit approach introduces no error for the transfer matrix. Quark-level effects manifest only through the nucleon NF coefficients, which we precompute once via build_nucleon_nf.
